dedupe_keys.name: germany s seveso iii directive article 21 report for 2019 2022 bmuv

description: This is Germany's report to the European Commission under Article 21(2) and (5) of Directive 2012/18/EU (Seveso III) on the control of major-accident hazards involving dangerous substances, covering 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2022. It answers the Commission's questionnaire set by Implementing Decision C(2014) 9335, describing the competent federal and state authorities and their tasks, such as evaluating safety reports, controlling land use near establishments, domino effects, external emergency plans, inspections, public information and penalties, along with the legislation that implements the directive and how it is applied. It is published by the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation, Nuclear Safety and Consumer Protection (BMUV), dated 30 September 2023. Coverage is national, with differences between the federal states noted. The report is a free PDF in German. Caveats: it follows a fixed questionnaire, so detail on individual establishments and accidents is limited, and the pages read give no licence; federal structures mean practice differs between states. For simulation it documents the regulatory framework that shapes emergency planning, land use separation and domino effect rules around chemical sites, useful for setting scenarios in emergency response and resilience studies. It is related to the JRC emergency response planning for chemical accident hazards record in this catalogue.
